report.headline: ALLHAT-LLT failed to demonstrate a mortality benefit with pravastatin because the placebo-adjusted LDL-C reduction of only 9.6% yielded insufficient power (12.9%) for the overall mortality endpoint.
report.summary: The trial randomized 10,355 hypertensive patients to pravastatin or usual care with a primary endpoint of overall mortality. The placebo-adjusted LDL-C reduction was only -9.6% at 4 years (pravastatin -17.2% vs usual care -7.6%), far smaller than typical statin trials. This translated to an expected hazard ratio of 0.955 (4.5% relative risk reduction) but the trial had only 12.9% power to detect this effect given 1,272 deaths over 4.8 years of follow-up; the minimum detectable HR for 80% power was 0.855. The trial's own readout stated the cholesterol difference was too small to show a mortality difference. The calculator predicted failure with 13% success probability, consistent with the observed result.
key_evidence: Placebo-adjusted LDL-C reduction: -9.6% (source: NHLBI Study Finds Traditional Diuretics Better Than Newer Medicines for Treating Hypertension (NIH News Release, includes ALLHAT cholesterol-lowering trial results))

report.what_would_change_this: A larger LDL-C difference (e.g., 25-35% placebo-adjusted reduction typical of statin trials) or a CHD-specific endpoint in a higher-risk population would have provided adequate power; the usual care comparator allowing crossover (evidenced by -7.6% LDL-C reduction in control) fundamentally limited the achievable treatment difference.
report.readthrough_note: The LIPID trial in secondary prevention demonstrated clear benefit with pravastatin 40 mg (HR 0.76 for CHD death), confirming HMGCR target causality in an appropriate population; subsequent genetic evidence (post-2002) further supports target validity.

issues.issue: Calculator inputs missing observed_hr and observed_ci despite available event counts (631 vs 641 deaths). Observed HR ≈ 0.984 can be calculated and should be included for completeness and to enable consistency check.
issues.request: Add observed_hr: 0.984 (or 631/641) and observed_ci if available from trial publication to calculator inputs.

issues.issue: Baseline LDL-C assumption of 2.0 mmol/L (77 mg/dL) may be too low for ALLHAT-LLT population (primary prevention, hypertensive patients with moderately elevated cholesterol). LIPID baseline was 135 mg/dL (3.5 mmol/L); SHIPS baseline 280 mg/dL. The absolute LDL-C change (0.192 mmol/L) and expected_hr (0.955) depend on this assumption.
issues.request: Search for ALLHAT-LLT baseline LDL-C in trial publication (JAMA 2002;288:2998) or CT.gov records to replace assumed value with verified fact.

issues.issue: Pravastatin dose in ALLHAT-LLT not specified in verified facts. Hypothesis 'design_or_endpoint' references 'pravastatin 40mg' by comparison to LIPID, but dose for ALLHAT-LLT is unconfirmed in provided facts.
issues.request: Search for pravastatin dose in ALLHAT-LLT (CT.gov NCT00000542, JAMA 2002 publication) to confirm dose used.
